title: Join road generation and settlement planting so roads do not terminate in walls

decision.which_side_yields: ROADS. Routing consumes the settlement plan; buildings never move.
why: ARBITRATION S28 already ruled the axis: 'settlement positions are authoritative and immovable, but the route between any two of them may be re-cut freely'. That is binding and it names roads as the yielding side.
planSettlement()'s own contract says positions are RI-WLD03 R4's spatial proof of the town's power reading and are NEVER moved. Moving a building changes what the town means.
tools/world/build-settlements.mjs is claimed by another live piece (W1-15-r3 lineage); tools/world/build-roads.mjs is not.

Buildings-avoid-roads would have to run inside planSettlement(), a PURE runtime function, which would then need the road network at plan time - a heavier coupling than a build-time generator reading a data file.
decision.shape: Not a detour around towns. A local lateral THREAD: the finished leg polyline is pushed the minimum distance needed to leave every building footprint, so the road runs BETWEEN the houses and becomes a street inside the town. Length change is metres, not kilometres.

findings.text: tools/world/road-through-building.mjs calls planSettlement(doc, {}) - it passes an EMPTY interiors map. The running game calls setSettlements(docs, this.data.interiors) with all 115 interiors. 114 of 202 buildings get a DIFFERENT footprint between the two, and the game's is often bigger: stormhold-scribe is 10.0x11.5 m to the check and 12.4x14.4 m to the body. A road cleared against the check's footprints is not necessarily cleared against the body's walls. My join therefore clears the UNION of both footprints, which makes the instrument's number sound rather than optimistic. I have NOT modified the instrument (it belongs to W1-01-r4 and the brief says do not rebuild it).

notes: The road-through-building --self-test now FAILS, and correctly so: its positive arm A was the shipped defect (stormhold-scribe across stormhold-helstrom). With the join in, arm A is clean, so the self-test as written cannot pass on a fixed tree. Its own error message anticipates this ("retarget this test"). I have NOT edited it (it is W1-01-r4s file and the brief says do not rebuild it); tools/world/road-join-consumption.mjs re-runs the same flag/clear/everything-else-identical logic against a building that IS on the new road, which is the retargeted arm A.

RULE 17 IN THE WILD: eight successive orchestrator banks (git add -A) between 02:17Z and 02:31Z committed tools/world/build-roads.mjs and game/data/world/roads.json MID-EDIT under other agents messages. git log -- <path> therefore names commits that already carry half of this change; the delete-the-fix base had to be found by grepping every recent commit for the task id. Base is 69e6ffa (02:15:23Z), the last revision with no W1-ROAD-JOIN marker.

The NULL control found a real defect in my own join and I changed the design because of it. The re-cut zone was originally scoped BY TOWN, with the radius taken from the town plus its farthest building; moving one outbuilding 800 m out inflated Stormholds zone to 845 m, swallowed most of two legs into one fine-grid solve and moved the road 236 m for a perturbation that should have moved it none. The zone is now scoped by ROAD PROXIMITY TO ANY BUILDING (INFLUENCE_M = 55 m), which is both more robust and simpler. The null now reads 0.00 m.

The P3-GROW perturbation initially did not bite and looked like a coupling failure. It was not: planSettlement()s shrink pass caught the enlarged building swallowing its neighbours centres and shrank both parties back, so the model legally undid the edit. The probe now searches (building, factor) in memory for a growth whose EFFECTIVE post-shrink footprint reaches the road, and reports the effective footprint. Worth knowing for anyone else perturbing settlement footprints.
